title: Manage-sell-offer with offer ID 2^53+1 passed as a decimal string: encoded exactly
caps_note: offerID has been an int64 since the first protocol; the rule is in the XDR definitions and stellar-core's ManageOffer validation, not in a CAP.
why: The control of the unsafe-number vector: 2^53+1 is a valid offer ID, and passed as a decimal string it is never rounded, so every SDK that takes a string ID must encode exactly 9007199254740993. A refusal or another ID here means the defect is in the string path, not in JavaScript's number type.
notes: Built by xdrcheck-corpus synth from corpus/recipes/classic/api-offer-id-encoding.id-2-pow-53-plus-1-string.json. The expected Operation XDR is the one of classic/api-offer-id-encoding.id-2-pow-53-plus-1-number (no source; MANAGE_SELL_OFFER; selling native; buying USD:GA7QYNF7…; amount 10000000 stroops; price 1/1) with offer ID 9007199254740993 (0x0020000000000001), computed from the XDR definitions with an independent encoder; no SDK output was used. An SDK whose offer-ID parameter is declared as an integer only (Python's stellar-sdk annotates offer_id as int) cannot take a string: its cell is n_a (argument_type_not_accepted, docs/conformance-protocol.md).
